key_incentives: ["Innovation Labs/CoEs: govt funds up to 40% of capex, max INR 5 crore (Bengaluru Urban); up to 75% of capex, max INR 3 crore Beyond Bengaluru", "Rental reimbursement (Beyond Bengaluru, first year): 50% of rent up to INR 50 lakh (100+ employees) or up to INR 2 crore (500+ employees)", "Recruitment assistance (Beyond Bengaluru): 10-50% of recruitment cost by hiring slab, caps INR 35 lakh to INR 7 crore; customised package for 1,000+ hires", "EPF reimbursement (Beyond Bengaluru, new GCCs with 100+ staff): up to INR 3,000/month/employee for 2 years, for up to 30% of workforce (max 250 employees)", "R&D infrastructure grant: up to 40% of approved budget or INR 50 crore, whichever is lower (max 3 GCCs Beyond Bengaluru)", "Skilling: 20% reimbursement up to INR 36,000 per graduate / INR 18,000 per diploma holder; internship stipend 50% up to INR 5,000/month for 3 months", "100% electricity duty reimbursement for 5 years; 30% property tax reimbursement for 3 years; 25% of internet expenses up to INR 12 lakh/yr for 3 years (Beyond Bengaluru)", "Co-working seats Beyond Bengaluru: 75%/50%/25% of vacant seat cost over 3 years, max INR 6,000/seat and INR 2.16 crore per applicant", "Startups using GCC labs: 100% reimbursement up to INR 40 lakh per GCC; quality certification 50% up to INR 6 lakh; patent fees 50% up to INR 2 lakh (domestic)"]
targets: 500 new GCCs (1,000 total) by 2029, 3.5 lakh new jobs, US$50 billion economic output
summary: Announced in November 2024 and described as India's first dedicated GCC policy, it aims to double Karnataka's GCC base to 1,000 by 2029. Most cost-side incentives (rent, EPF, recruitment, power, property tax) are reserved for 'Beyond Bengaluru' clusters, while Bengaluru gets innovation-lab, skilling and R&D support.

key_incentives: ["Incentives for IT parks, data centres and incubation centres (amounts not found in sources)", "Workforce skill-training support", "TG-iPASS single-window clearance with 15-day deemed approval"]
summary: No notified standalone GCC policy appears on Telangana's IT department or Invest Telangana policy pages; GCCs are covered by the ICT Policy 2021-26 plus TG-iPASS fast approvals. The state reports 500+ GCCs and is building IT hubs/towers in Tier-II cities such as Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam and Nizamabad (a nasscom article describes Telangana's GCC approach as a 'policy', but no document was found).

key_incentives: ["Capital subsidy: 20% of eligible fixed capital investment, capped at INR 10 crore (Small) / 20 crore (Medium) / 50 crore (Large) / 100 crore (Mega), paid in 5 instalments", "Rental assistance (new units, 5 years, in lieu of capital subsidy): 10% of rent in Zone I (MMR/PMR), 20% in Zone II; caps INR 1-4 crore by unit size", "Payroll subsidy (3 years): 40% of salary (Zone I) / 50% (Zone II), max INR 50,000 per employee, 100 employees, INR 5 crore per unit; employees earning > INR 1 lakh/month", "Stamp duty exemption: 100% (SEZ/STPI), 75% (public IT park), 50% (private IT park)", "Power tariff subsidy INR 1/unit (Zone I) or INR 2/unit (other zones) for 5 years, cap INR 20 lakh/unit/year; 100% electricity duty exemption for 10 years", "R&D grant 25% up to INR 2 crore; patent filing 50% up to INR 50 lakh; internship support up to INR 10,000/month per intern (max 100)", "Interest subsidy (Zone II only, 5 years): interest above 5% on term loans, yearly cap INR 5 crore", "Non-fiscal: industry status, 24x7 operations, 10% of new MIDC land reserved for GCCs, additional FSI; customised package for >INR 750 crore or >1,000 jobs"]
targets: 400 new GCCs, 4 lakh high-skilled jobs and INR 50,600 crore investment (2025-2030)
summary: Approved by the state cabinet in September 2025, the policy offers size-graded capital, rental, payroll and power incentives to GCCs. Zone II (outside Mumbai and Pune) gets higher rental and payroll rates plus an interest subsidy, to push growth into Nagpur, Nashik and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

policy_name: Special Scheme to promote Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in Tamil Nadu (G.O. Ms. No. 34, 2024)
key_incentives: ["Payroll subsidy on high-paying jobs (>= INR 1 lakh/month basic wages): 30% in year 1, 20% in year 2, 10% in year 3", "Eligibility: Forbes Global 2000 / Fortune 1000 companies (exceptions via Inter Departmental Committee), minimum 200 direct jobs; subsidy only for TN-domiciled employees", "Subsidy limited to 50 GCCs during the scheme period (1 April 2024 - 31 March 2027); disbursed by SIPCOT"]
summary: Tamil Nadu has no comprehensive GCC policy document but notified a dedicated GCC payroll-subsidy scheme in March 2024 following the 2024-25 Budget, which also committed to facilitating GCCs in Coimbatore and Madurai. Other relevant instruments are the TN IT Policy 2018 and TN R&D Policy 2022.

No dedicated GCC policy was found on Haryana's IT department site; the IT & ESDM Policy 2017 (amended up to 2019) remains the listed IT policy, alongside the State Data Centre Policy 2022 and Startup Policy 2022. Incentive amounts could not be verified from sources.

key_incentives: ["Land subsidy: 30% (Gautam Buddha Nagar & Ghaziabad), 40% (Paschimanchal & Madhyanchal), 50% (Poorvanchal & Bundelkhand)", "100% stamp duty exemption/reimbursement on land/office space purchase", "Capital subsidy: 25% of eligible investment, max INR 10 crore (Level-1) / INR 25 crore (Advanced GCC), over 7 years", "Operational subsidy: 20% of rent, bandwidth, power and data-centre costs, max INR 40 crore/yr (Level-1) / INR 80 crore/yr (Advanced) for 5 years", "Payroll reimbursement up to 3 years (25-50% by region), max INR 10 crore/yr (Level-1) / INR 20 crore/yr (Advanced); up to INR 1.8 lakh per employee", "Interest subsidy 5% on term loans up to INR 1 crore/yr for 5 years; SGST reimbursement", "INR 20,000 per fresher hired from UP institutions; 100% EPF reimbursement for women, SC/ST, transgender and disabled employees (cap INR 1 crore/yr, 3 years)", "R&D/CoE grants up to INR 10 crore; patent cost reimbursement up to INR 5 lakh (domestic) / INR 10 lakh (international)", "Customised packages for Fortune 500 / India top-500 companies or FDI above INR 100 crore"]
targets: Over 2 lakh jobs in five years
summary: UP's dedicated GCC policy targets Fortune 500 and large firms with land, capital, operating and payroll subsidies, graded by GCC level (Level-1 vs Advanced). Higher land subsidies in eastern and Bundelkhand regions and a push for Lucknow, Kanpur and Varanasi alongside Noida give it a clear Tier-2 tilt.

key_incentives: ["CAPEX subsidy: 20% of eligible non-IT infrastructure capex and 30% of IT investments; max INR 50 crore (GFCI < INR 250 crore) or INR 200 crore (Mega: GFCI >= INR 250 crore or 500+ employees); paid in 20 quarterly instalments", "OPEX subsidy: 15% of annual operating costs (lease rent, bandwidth, cloud, power), capped at INR 20 crore/yr (Category I) or INR 40 crore/yr (Mega) for 5 years", "Employment assistance: one-time 50% of one month's CTC for new local hires, cap INR 50,000 (male) / INR 60,000 (female)", "EPF reimbursement: 100% for female, 75% for male employees", "Interest subsidy 7% on term loans (cap INR 1 crore); full electricity duty reimbursement", "Patent assistance up to INR 10 lakh per patent (up to 10 patents/yr); quality certification up to 80% of cost (max INR 10 lakh)", "Skilling: up to 50% course-fee reimbursement for professionals and 75% for students"]
targets: 250+ new GCC units, 50,000+ jobs, INR 10,000 crore investment by 2030
summary: Launched at GIFT City in February 2025 and valid to 31 March 2030, the policy offers some of the largest capex/opex caps of any state (up to INR 200 crore capex for mega GCCs) to units with at least 50 employees. Sources reviewed did not describe a specific Tier-2 city carve-out; GIFT City IFSC benefits are pitched alongside.

key_incentives: ["SGST reimbursement on eligible expenses, max INR 10 crore over 5 years", "Up to 100% stamp duty and registration waiver in designated IT parks; up to 50% waiver of land conversion charges", "Property tax waived for 5 years for all GCC office spaces; 50% land-tax reimbursement for 5 years for private IT parks", "Capital subsidy for office infrastructure with min INR 50 crore investment and 1,000 jobs; total disbursal max INR 50 crore/yr across up to 10 investments", "Land lease premium subsidy: 5% (1,500+ jobs), 10% (2,500 jobs), 15% (4,000+ jobs)", "First six months' rent free in Infopark, Technopark and Cyberpark spaces; quality certification refund 50% up to INR 25 lakh/yr", "Rent discounts (5-10%) for diversity hiring and 50%+ women workforce in government IT parks"]
targets: Grow from 40 to 120 GCCs and from 40,000 to 2 lakh GCC jobs by 2030; 1.25 lakh AI/ML professionals; +20 million sq ft IT space
summary: Kerala has published a draft GCC policy (feedback window to May 2026) that pitches Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram as Tier-2 alternatives with a turnkey 'GCC Boilerplate' set-up service. It also promises special incentives for investments beyond those two cities; the policy is still a draft, not final.

key_incentives: ["Space allotment in 26 state IT parks via competitive bidding (from department site)", "Related policies: WB Data Centre Policy 2021 and WB Internet Cable Landing Station Policy 2023"]
summary: No GCC-specific policy was found for West Bengal; the IT & ITeS Policy 2018 is the latest IT policy listed by the state IT&E department. Specific fiscal incentive amounts were not verified from sources.

key_incentives: ["Under RIPS 2024 (min investment INR 5 crore): capital subsidy 30% of project cost (excl. land/building), max INR 10 crore over 10 years", "Land cost incentive: 50% of land purchase/floor-area lease cost up to INR 1 crore", "75% stamp duty exemption + 25% reimbursement; 100% electricity duty exemption for 7 years; 75% conversion charge exemption + 25% reimbursement", "Payroll subsidy (GCC Policy, first 10 GCCs per tier): 30% of salary for 3 years, cap INR 1.25 lakh per employee/yr and INR 10 crore per unit/yr", "Rental assistance: 50% of rent for 3 years then 25% for 2 years, max INR 5 crore/unit/yr and INR 25,000/seat/yr (only if land incentive not taken)", "Bandwidth: 25% of internet cost up to INR 25 lakh/yr for 3 years; training: 50% up to INR 30,000/employee and INR 2.5 crore/unit/yr for 3 years", "IP creation 50% up to INR 5 crore (R&D GCCs); green incentive 25% up to INR 1 crore; customised package for 2,000+ jobs"]
summary: Rajasthan's dedicated GCC policy (valid to 31 March 2029) layers payroll, rental, bandwidth and training subsidies on top of the RIPS 2024 investment package. Eligibility for the extra GCC incentives is limited to the first 10 GCCs in each size tier (100+ / 500+ employees or INR 15 / 50 crore EFCI).

key_incentives: ["Capex subsidy: 40% of eligible capital investment, max INR 15 crore (Level-I/Category A) or INR 30 crore (Advanced/Category B), over 5 annual instalments", "Payroll subsidy for 3 years: 50% (Y1), 30% (Y2), 20% (Y3), capped at INR 1 lakh per employee per year (salary > INR 1 lakh)", "Rental / working capital assistance up to INR 3 crore (Level-I) / INR 10 crore (Advanced)", "Interest assistance 6% up to INR 5 crore; 100% stamp duty and registration reimbursement; land rebate up to 75%", "Upskilling INR 50,000 per employee or 50% of cost; R&D 50% reimbursement up to INR 1 crore/yr; internship support INR 10,000 per intern", "Quality certification 50% up to INR 6 lakh; event hosting up to INR 25 lakh/yr"]
summary: Launched in February 2025, MP's GCC policy is framed as India's first framework to grow GCCs in Tier-2 cities (Indore, Bhopal, Jabalpur), with MPSeDC as nodal agency. Eligibility tiers are Level-I (INR 15 crore capex or 100 staff) and Advanced (INR 50 crore or 250 staff).

key_incentives: ["State cites capex/opex subsidy, interest reimbursement, lease rental subsidies and performance-linked grants for employment and exports (amounts not found)", "Industrial power tariff cited at INR 5.5/unit; GCC parks and tech parks planned in Tier-2/3 cities"]
targets: Draft Digital Economy Vision 2030: 100+ GCCs; 3 GCC hubs attracting INR 7,500+ crore and 1 lakh jobs by 2036
summary: Odisha's E&IT department notified a new IT Policy in November 2025 (gazette not reviewed), and its draft Digital Economy Vision 2030 lists a GCC policy as 'upcoming'. The vision positions Bhubaneswar and Rourkela as lower-cost Tier-2 GCC hubs.

key_incentives: ["Direct financial support (amounts not found in sources)", "Infrastructure models for MSMEs, IT parks and hybrid/co-working workspaces under a three-tier infrastructure approach"]
summary: A nasscom review lists Andhra Pradesh among six states with dedicated GCC policies for 2024-2029, aligned to the Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 and emphasising co-working, IT campuses and hybrid workspaces. The exact policy title, year and incentive amounts could not be verified from an official source.
No dedicated GCC policy or current IT/ITeS policy details for Punjab or Chandigarh could be verified from accessible sources. Treat as unknown.
